To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heat‐denaturation method can be used for the measurement of HIV‐1 p24124 antigen by FC.
the ultrasensitive heat‐mediated format for HIV p24 detection can be applied to a FC platform and that this format is applicable to a broad spectrum of HIV subtypes.
the principle of HIV‐1 p‐24 antigen detection using the heat denaturation format can be applied in a flow cytometric assay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel HIV diagnostic assay, which is based on flow cytometry.
the development of an HIV microsphere immuno‐assay (Mia) that could be used in a flow cytometer for the quantification of HIV p 24.
the development of an HIV microsphere‐based immunoassay for the detection of HIV‐1 p 24 antigen in human plasma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HIV‐1 P24 antigen can be measured in a microsphere‐immunoassay (Biomaric) using a flow cytometer (FC).
this study is a proof‐of‐principle for the development of an ultrasensitive HIV‐1 p‐24 antigen microsphere‐based immunoassay.
this assay is not ready for clinical use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HIV‐1 antigen, p24, can be quantified using a MIA and FC.
the ultrasensitive Biomariac p24 MIA has a potential for HIV clinical diagnosis.
we developed a novel ultrasensitive p24 FC‐based assay that could have potential application in resource‐poored settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a p24 microspheres immunoassay can be developed and applied to flow cytometric detection.
the principle of HIV‐1 p 24 detection by FC using the ultrasensitive heat‐denature format is feasible.
we have shown for the first time that the principle of the ultrasensitive p24 assay can be applied to flow cytometry.
